reason: The hypothesis relies on strain-induced d-band center shifts to tune adsorption, but the cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) does not directly support tensile strain from annealing in PtCuCo HEAs or its effect on ethanol oxidation. E1 discusses N-doping and lattice expansion in a different system, E2 and E3 describe PdCuCo nanoalloys with compressive strain and downshifted d-band centers, not tensile strain. The key premise linking annealing to tensile strain and improved ethanol oxidation is unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Tensile lattice strain in Pt-based alloys can shift the d-band center of surface atoms.
A downshifted d-band center weakens adsorption of poisoning intermediates, enhancing catalytic activity.
Dendritic PdCuCo nanoalloys exhibit high activity and durability due to d-band center shifts and strain effects.
Thermal annealing can induce controlled tensile strain without altering nanocrystal morphology.
Optimized intermediate adsorption energies improve ethanol oxidation selectivity and durability.
